title: Use one language and named entities
intent: Keep credibility and mechanical cleanliness by removing stock names and mixed languages from shipped copy.
when_to_use: the page names customers, people, or companies in shipped copy
the artifact declares a language and the audience is single language
when_not_to_use: the artifact is a fixture or demo where stock names are expected and the file is marked as a fixture
the page is deliberately bilingual and states that on the page
rules: the copy contains no Jane Doe, John Doe, Acme, Nexus, SmartFlow, or Lorem ipsum
the declared lang matches the dominant language of the visible copy, including alt text, aria labels, and button text
the copy contains no em-dash and no en-dash; ranges and asides use a hyphen, a comma, or a colon
every named customer, person, or company exists and is permitted to be named, or the name is removed and the claim weakened to what can be supported
trade_off: Real names need permission and review, and removing them weakens proof sections, so some sections shrink instead of shipping with placeholders that everyone has learned to ignore.
failure_mode: One stock name survives in a testimonial, an alt attribute, or an aria label after the visible copy is cleaned, which is exactly where the tell is machine checked.

example.brief: SaaS landing page that needs social proof.
example.ruling: Two placeholder testimonials are cut rather than renamed, the surviving quote keeps its real author and role, lang matches the copy, and every numeric range is rewritten with a hyphen.
